evidence.note: The lead carries a genuine tier-1 primary (digitaleconomy.stanford.edu, read directly — methodology, named researchers, exact figures) plus independent tier-2 confirmation (Forbes, same figures, same authors, published the same day as the primary). The top story (Bill Gates) rests on two tier-2 outlets with distinct framing — MIT Technology Review's interview transcript versus Fortune's three-risks framing — rather than one wire item run twice. Every standard/brief has at least one opened, real source; none is fabricated. Docked from 5 because six of ten stories run on a single tier-2 source, which is within the rules but thin, and because this draft itself shipped with 'confidence: high' on six stories whose best source was tier 2 — caught by validate.mjs, not by the drafting, and corrected to medium before this review.

Vendor claims are marked as claims: the Nvidia story states outright that the 30x figure is 'currently pending SemiAnalysis review' and that Nvidia's own post 'admits a core agentic capability isn't yet reflected,' with the whyItMatters explicitly telling the reader to wait for the independent review before treating the number as confirmed. The Stanford figures (15%->19%) are stated with their basis and cross-checked word-for-word against Forbes' independent write-up of the same study before use.

Bullets are facts throughout, e.g. the lead's third bullet: 'The adjustment operates through reduced hiring of young workers rather than increased separations of those already employed' states a mechanism, not a topic. The OpenAI whyItMatters ends on a concrete, arguable claim rather than a truism. Docked from 5 for two long compound sentences in the Nvidia body paragraph explaining the caveat chain.

The lead is close to unarguable: primary-sourced, data-driven, directly answers a question the paper's own readers ask (is AI actually taking jobs, and whose), and updates a widening trend rather than restating an old finding. No sub-$10m rounds ran (Ringg $10m, Stability $76m both clear the floor); the Nvidia vendor claim was not run uncritically. Nothing repeats editions 1-6.

Weakest dimension. Only one story (the lead) reached genuinely independent two-source status beyond the lead itself required; 'top' sits at 1 against a house range of 3-6 because nothing else cleared that bar honestly rather than being forced there. Policy is empty and Models is one short of quota; edition.summary states both plainly. No company dominates: OpenAI, Nvidia and Anthropic each appear once; business carries 3 of 10 stories, on the high side but not a majority.

revisions: Six stories shipped with confidence "high" on tier-2-only sourcing in the first draft; caught by validate.mjs and corrected to "medium" before this review, since "high" requires an actual tier-1 primary rather than confidence in tier-2 reporting.

Two standard stories (Ringg AI, IBM Granite 4.2) were drafted with summary-only content and no body or whyItMatters; caught by validate.mjs's schema check and given full three-paragraph bodies and a whyItMatters before this review, since prominence:"standard" requires both.
notes: node tools/validate.mjs returns 0 errors and 3 warnings, exit 0; --strict would block. All three are shape/quota warnings disclosed in edition.summary, none a sourcing defect.
